Info-ZIP Zip 3.0 (and 3.1 beta through 3.1c) allows OS command injection by an attacker who controls the command line. The victim must use the -T option followed by a filename containing shell metacharacters, on a platform (such as Linux) where a suitable shell is run. This occurs because the system C library function is used. NOTE: there is no known common scenario in which an untrusted filename reaches a zip -T call.

items.summary: Hello Everyone! We've just released Chrome 159 (159.0.8154.18) for Android to a small percentage of users. It'll become available on Google Play over the next few days. You can find more details about early Stable releases here . This release includes stability and performance improvements. You can see a full list of the changes in the Git log . On November 20, 2026, we released versions 19.6.1, 19.5.8, 19.4.10 for GitLab Community Edition and Enterprise Edition. These versions contain important bug and security fixes, and we strongly recommend that all self-managed GitLab installations be upgraded to
one of these versions immediately.
GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated are already running a patched version. GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated customers do not need to take action.
GitLab Dedicated was previously protected through internal-only releases 19.5.7 and 19.4.9, which contained interim mitigations for these vulnerabilities; all fixes from those releases are also included in 19.5.8 and 19.4.10. GitLab releases fixes for vulnerabilities in patch releases. There are two types of patch releases:
scheduled releases and ad-hoc critical patches for high-severity vulnerabilities. Scheduled releases are released twice a month on the second and fourth Wednesdays.
For more information, please visit our releases handbook and security FAQ .
You can see all of GitLab release blog posts here . We are committed to ensuring that all aspects of GitLab that are exposed to customers or that host customer data are held to
the highest security standards. To maintain good security hygiene, it is highly recommended that all customers
upgrade to the latest patch release for their supported version. You can read more best practices in securing your GitLab instance in our blog post. Recommended Action We strongly recommend that all installations running a version affected by the issues described below are upgraded to the latest version as soon as possible . When no specific deployment type (omnibus, source code, helm chart, etc.) of a product is mentioned, it means all types are affected. Important guidance for self-compiled GitLab installations: The fix for CVE-2026-132825 is a patch to Ruby. Official GitLab Linux packages and container images already include the patched Ruby. For self-compiled installations, you must rebuild the Ruby installation used to run GitLab with Ruby 3.3.14 or 3.4.13 (or a later release in the same minor series), which include the fixes for CVE-2026-132825 and the other vulnerabilities disclosed in the Ruby security advisory , as described in Ruby . Security fixes Table of security fixes Title Severity CVE-2026-132825 (vulnerability in ruby ) Critical The severity shown reflects the Critical rating assigned by the Ruby security team in GHSA-34m4-m9fh-gqp5 . MITRE rates CVE-2026-132825 as High (CVSS 7.4). As this is a vulnerability in Ruby rather than in GitLab’s own code, the severity is taken from the upstream advisory. CVE-2026-132825 (vulnerability in ruby ) This release addresses the security issue CVE-2026-132825 ( GHSA-34m4-m9fh-gqp5 ), a heap-based buffer overflow in the case conversion of strings in ruby , by updating the version of Ruby bundled with GitLab. This issue has been remediated on GitLab.com, and in GitLab CE/EE versions 19.4.10, 19.5.8, and 19.6.1. In GitLab, under certain conditions, changing the case of a crafted string can result in an out-of-bounds heap write. The Ruby security team has stated that this flaw may allow remote code execution in some scenarios. These versions also include fixes for all of the other vulnerabilities disclosed in the Ruby security advisory Multiple vulnerabilities in Regexp and String . Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions before 19.4.10, 19.5 before 19.5.8, and 19.6 before 19.6.1 Bug fixes 19.6.1 [19.6] Restore Ruby 3.3.12 regexp patches [19.6] Bump Ruby to 3.3.14 Backport 19.6 release notes to 19-6-stable-ee [19.6] Bump GITLAB_CNG_MIRROR_REF to restore Ruby 3.3.12 patches [19.6] Bump Ruby to 3.3.14 and 3.4.13 19.5.8 [19.5] Restore Ruby 3.3.12 regexp patches Backport of ‘Bump webauthn gem to 3.4.4’ Backport of ‘Count Geo secondary registries in a single pass’ [19.5] Bump GITLAB_CNG_MIRROR_REF to restore Ruby 3.3.12 patches Backport: Publish the Pulp repository if the uploaded RPM is not published (19-5) B
